dlg.dlg.abt-johannes.node.ch1.text: The abbey keeps its accounts of the March pastures carefully, {player}, charter by charter, since before your grandfather's grandfather. Schwyz keeps its own count of grievances just as carefully.
dlg.dlg.abt-johannes.node.ch2-other.text: We are excommunicate by our own bishop's word, {player}, and Schwyz still grazes where it pleases. I pray the arbitration your Bundesbrief promises is not only ink.
dlg.dlg.abt-johannes.node.ch2-other.vari: Excommunicate by our own bishop's word, {player} — and yet you heard me out at the gate when others would not. I have not forgotten it, whatever the bishop's clerks write of Schwyz.
Excommunicate, {player}, and my monks still wake dreaming of haltered wrists. Keep to your side of the March when you come here.
dlg.dlg.abt-johannes.node.negotiate-fail: Pretty words do not return grazing rights, {player}. Stand aside, or stand against us — the choice is not really mine to make gentle.
dlg.dlg.abt-johannes.node.negotiate-succ: You argue like a man who has read the Bundesbrief's own clause on arbitration. Very well — I will not bar the gate, but this is not forgiveness, only patience.
dlg.dlg.abt-johannes.node.negotiate.choi: "Charters can be read more than one way, Vater Abt."
Say nothing, and let the men behind you speak instead.
dlg.dlg.abt-johannes.node.negotiate.text: "Vater Abt" is a courtesy you still extend me, I notice, even with Schwyz men at my gate. The March pastures are the abbey's by charter, {player} — I did not invent that title, only inherited it.
dlg.dlg.alpstreit-dispute.node.agree.tex: "The Bundesbrief itself says a quarrel among us goes to judgment before the sword. Let's see if that's more than ink."
dlg.dlg.alpstreit-dispute.node.dispute.c: Hear him out, and offer to arbitrate.
"Boundary stones are the Landsgemeinde's business, not mine."
dlg.dlg.alpstreit-dispute.node.dispute.t: The farmer points up-slope with his staff. "The Arth herders have moved their boundary stones again, {player} — a stone's throw further onto Schwyz grass every summer, and I'm tired of arguing it myself."
dlg.dlg.alpstreit-hearing.node.hearing.c: Weigh the claims fairly and rule.
Divide the disputed ground by the old stones and have done.
dlg.dlg.alpstreit-hearing.node.hearing.t: Both sides lay their claims before you on the disputed slope — old boundary stones, half-remembered grazing rights, and no small amount of pride.
dlg.dlg.alpstreit-hearing.node.ruling-ac: Your judgment — the boundary restored to the old stones, with both herds granted a fair week's grazing each on the disputed ground — satisfies neither side entirely, which the elders tell you is the surest sign of a fair ruling.
dlg.dlg.alpstreit-hearing.node.ruling-re: Your ruling satisfies no one, and the Arth herders mutter about moving the stones back the moment your back is turned. Still, blood was not drawn over it — for now.
dlg.dlg.arnold-von-melchtal.node.ch1.cho: Vengeance is a heavy thing to carry.
dlg.dlg.arnold-von-melchtal.node.ch1.tex: My father cannot see the alp he tended his whole life, {player}, because a bailiff's man took his eyes for it. Tell me I am wrong to want the Vogt gone.
dlg.dlg.arnold-von-melchtal.node.ch1.var: You keep good company these days — a man who puts a bolt exactly where he means to.
You stood in the square and watched Tell refuse, {player}? My father would have paid his last goat to see that morning.
dlg.dlg.arnold-von-melchtal.node.ch2.tex: My halberd is sharp and my father still cannot see me carry it. That will have to be enough reason for Morgarten.
dlg.dlg.arnold-von-melchtal.node.prologu: A young Obwalden herdsman, driving a few goats down off the Melchtal alp before the weather turns. "Word is a King has died, {player}," he says. "My father says that changes little for men like us. I am not so sure."
dlg.dlg.bad-wolfenschiessen-hide.node.hi: By first light there is nothing left to find, and the household's story is straight enough to survive any clerk's questions.
It is done, but not so cleanly that a sharp-eyed clerk would find nothing at all — a risk the household will simply have to live with.
Do the plain work and leave the fine details be.
Between the burial by lantern-light and the story the household will tell if anyone from Sarnen comes asking, there is a great deal that wants doing quietly before dawn.
dlg.dlg.bad-wolfenschiessen.node.agree.t: "Then there's a body wants a quiet grave and a story wants a quiet ending, before some clerk from Landenberg's hill comes asking questions we'd rather not answer."
"I can keep a silence as well as anyone."
"I want no part in buried secrets, Jost."

Jost lowers his voice, though there's no one else in the yard. "You'll have heard, maybe, that the bailiff's man who troubled a certain house here won't be troubling anyone again. What you haven't heard is best kept that way, {player}."
dlg.dlg.beringer-von-landenberg.node.ch1: "Curiosity about your New Year custom, Herr Vogt."
"Sarnen pays its dues on time, which is more than I can say for half this valley." The bailiff studies you. "What brings a stranger to my hill?"
dlg.dlg.bruder-anselm.node.companion.tex: I can read you any charter you like, {player}, in the original Latin or plain speech — a useful thing to have along, whatever else I am.
dlg.dlg.bruder-anselm.node.conflicted.te: They are monks, {player}, whatever quarrel Schwyz has with their abbot. I will stand with you tonight, but do not ask me to enjoy it.
dlg.dlg.bruder-anselm.node.recruit.choic: Stay with your books for now.
dlg.dlg.bruder-anselm.node.recruit.text: A lay brother with ink-stained fingers, restless in his habit. "Engelberg feeds and clothes me, {player}, and asks in return that I stay put. I am beginning to think I was made for the road instead."
dlg.dlg.burgenbruch-council.node.council: It is done, but not cleanly — Rotzberg's garrison gets a warning shout off before the rope party is inside, and there is a wound or two to show for it by the time word reaches you.
Climb Rotzberg by rope, yourself, by night.
Join the New Year's gift procession into Sarnen yourself.
Send trusted companions to all three, and command from Altdorf.

Word goes round the valleys: before spring, Zwing Uri, Rotzberg and Landenberg's hill at Sarnen must all fall. "One of us should see it done with our own hands," someone says. "The rest can be trusted to good men."
dlg.dlg.burgenbruch-council.node.delegat: Word comes back within days, each messenger arriving grinning and travel-worn. At Zwing Uri, the labourers' file carried its hidden halberds through the unfinished gate and the half-built keep surrendered before dawn. At Rotzberg, a rope dropped from a high window let the climbers over the wall while the garrison slept, and the servant girl's part in it is already half a song. At Sarnen, the New Year's gift baskets opened on Landenberg's own doorstep, and the hill was taken before he found his sword. All three, and barely a scratch between the lot of them.
dlg.dlg.drache-pilatus-truth.node.smuggl: The smuggler surrenders without a fight once he sees he's cornered — and hands over a share of the cache to keep the matter quiet.
He bolts down a scree slope before you can close the distance — gone, but so is the mystery. A lammergeier, and a smuggler's empty cache. No dragon.
dlg.dlg.drache-pilatus-truth.node.summit: Catch the smuggler quietly rather than raise an alarm.
Mark the cache and climb back down to report it.

High on the Pilatus alp, the "dragon" reveals itself: a lammergeier, vast wingspan and all, stooping on goats same as any bearded vulture — and, tucked in a hollow below its favoured cliff, a smuggler's cache of untaxed salt.
dlg.dlg.drache-pilatus.node.agree.text: "Bless you. Whatever it is, it's been unsettling the herders — and I'd sleep easier not hearing about it over every cup I pour."
dlg.dlg.drache-pilatus.node.rumour.choic: Offer to go look into it.
"Dragons keep to their mountains, and I to my road."
dlg.dlg.drache-pilatus.node.rumour.text: The innkeeper leans in, lowering her voice the way tavern-keepers do before the best gossip. "They say a dragon's been seen circling Pilatus again, {player} — a brother from the mountain swears he saw it stoop on a goat."
dlg.dlg.fischer-gersau-confront.node.con: "Free village or not, the road's the bailiff's road." He won't budge — but he does agree, grudgingly, to stop harassing the smaller carts.
He grumbles, but the fish carts roll past unmolested from that day on — a small victory, but Gersau will remember it.
"Gersau owes no lord a toll, and you know it."
Pay him off quietly (5 Pfennig) to leave Gersau be.
Leave him to his ledger — for now.
The toll-man looks up from his ledger, unbothered. "Gersau pays the shore toll like everyone else who wants to keep their fish."
dlg.dlg.fischer-gersau.node.agree.text: "Bei Sankt Verena, someone finally willing to say something. His name's Konrad Niederberger — you'll find him at the Brunnen quay road, self-important as a bishop."
dlg.dlg.fischer-gersau.node.trouble.choi: Offer to speak to the toll collector.
"Toll-men and fish carts are none of my affair."
dlg.dlg.fischer-gersau.node.trouble.text: "We're a free village, {player}, answer to no lord — and still the Brunnen toll-men stop our fish carts on the shore road as if we owed them something." The fisherman spits into the lake for emphasis.
dlg.dlg.generic.boatman.node.talk.text: "Crossing, or just admiring the boat?" The boatman rests an oar across his knees. "I know this lake's temper better than my own wife's — say the word and I'll row you across."
dlg.dlg.generic.child.node.talk.text: A child stares up at you, more curious about your weapon than your errand. "Are you a soldier? Have you killed anyone? Mother says I'm not to ask that."
dlg.dlg.generic.elder.node.opinion.text: "Things were simpler before the bailiffs, and harder before that, and simpler still before the harder times. An old man's memory smooths a great deal, mind you."
dlg.dlg.generic.elder.node.talk.text: An old man of the Landsgemeinde nods slowly at you. "I've sat through more meadow-meetings than I care to count. Ask an old man's opinion and you'll get one, free of charge."
dlg.dlg.generic.habsburg-guard.node.host: "You." The guardsman's hand does not leave his sword hilt. "The Landvogt keeps a list of names like yours, and mine goes on it too if I let you linger. Be elsewhere."
dlg.dlg.generic.habsburg-guard.node.neut: "Keep the peace and you'll have no trouble from me." The Habsburg guard nods you past his post.
dlg.dlg.generic.habsburg-guard.node.wary: "State your business." The guard looks you over the way a man looks over a debt he suspects won't be paid.
dlg.dlg.generic.herder.node.alps.text: "Higher up, the grass is better but the weather turns without warning. Mind the mist if you go — a man can walk off an edge he never saw."
dlg.dlg.generic.herder.node.talk.text: A herder leans on a staff, watching cattle pick their way up a slope. "Good grazing this year, God willing it stays that way. You're not from these parts, by your boots."
dlg.dlg.generic.innkeeper.node.gossip.te: "Same as always — tolls too high, harvest too thin, and the bailiff's men drinking on credit they never mean to settle."
dlg.dlg.generic.innkeeper.node.talk.text: "Sit, if you're paying — stand if you're only asking questions." The innkeeper wipes a cup that was already clean. "Bread's two Pfennig, and worth every Haller of it, if I do say so."
dlg.dlg.generic.innkeeper.node.thanks.te: "Mind the crust — baked this morning, still has some bite to it."
dlg.dlg.generic.merchant.node.prices.tex: "Higher past every toll station, naturally. A Zürich Pfund buys less at Küssnacht than it does at Schwyz — the bailiffs see to that."
dlg.dlg.generic.merchant.node.talk.choic: Ask about prices on the road.
dlg.dlg.generic.merchant.node.talk.text: "Cloth, salt, a little cheese if you've the coin for Alpkäse — I carry what sells between here and Luzern." The trader eyes your purse rather than your face.
dlg.dlg.generic.monk.node.business.text: "Charters, mostly — who owns what pasture, what forest, what right of way. Dull work, until someone decides it isn't."
dlg.dlg.generic.monk.node.talk.text: "Pax vobiscum." The brother inclines his head. "We keep the hours here whatever the valley below is arguing about this week."
dlg.dlg.generic.peasant.node.news.text: "Nothing much changes here — the bailiff's toll, the weather, and whose cow got into whose barley. You'd know more from the tavern than from me."
dlg.dlg.generic.peasant.node.talk.choice: Bid them good day and move on.
dlg.dlg.generic.peasant.node.talk.text: A field-worker straightens up from the furrow, glad of the excuse to rest a moment. "Fair day for it, or fair enough. What brings you off the road?"
Ask for a blessing on the road ahead.
dlg.dlg.generic.priest.node.talk.text: "Bei Sankt Verena, a new face at Mass." The priest folds his hands. "Are you come for confession, for counsel, or only out of the rain?"
dlg.dlg.generic.saeumer.node.coop.text: "We look after our own on that road — share the tolls, share the losses when a mule goes over the edge. It's the only way the pass gets crossed at all, some seasons."
dlg.dlg.generic.saeumer.node.talk.text: A muleteer checks a girth strap without looking up. "Gotthard road's clear as far as Amsteg, muddy past it. Mind the tolls — they multiply the higher you climb."
dlg.dlg.generic.toll-collector.node.talk: "Toll's due, unless you fancy fording upstream instead." The collector holds out an open palm without much hope of refusal.
dlg.dlg.generic.toll-collector.node.toll: "No coin, no crossing." He plants himself squarely in your path until you produce it.
dlg.dlg.gessler-hat.node.after-fight.tex: The square empties around the fight's aftermath — word of it will reach the Vogt within the hour, one way or another.
dlg.dlg.gessler-hat.node.bowed.text: The clerk marks something in his ledger and loses interest in you at once. Around the square, a few Uri faces turn away.
dlg.dlg.gessler-hat.node.confronted.choi: Offer him twenty Pfennig to forget he saw you.
Put a hand to your weapon instead.
dlg.dlg.gessler-hat.node.confronted.text: "You. Yes, you — I watched you walk right past the Landvogt's hat as if it were a scarecrow." He raises two fingers, and men-at-arms drift closer. "Explain yourself, or don't."
dlg.dlg.gessler-hat.node.fight.text: The guards close in before you can say another word.
dlg.dlg.gessler-hat.node.pole.choice.0: Bow to the hat, as the proclamation demands.
dlg.dlg.gessler-hat.node.pole.choice.2: Hang back at the square's edge and watch.
dlg.dlg.gessler-hat.node.pole.text: By the lime tree in Altdorf's square, a pole stands hung with a Habsburg hat, and Vogt-Schreiber Ludwig loiters near it with a ledger, watching who bows and who does not.
dlg.dlg.gessler-hat.node.released.text: "Mind the pole next time." He waves the guards back, disappointed.
dlg.dlg.gessler-hat.node.watch-tell.text: A crossbowman in worn hunting leathers walks past the pole without so much as a glance at it. The guards are on him in a breath. "Wilhelm Tell of Bürglen does not bow to a hat on a stick," he says, loud enough for the square to hear.
dlg.dlg.heini-odermatt.node.companion.te: Just don't leave me alone on a flank, {player}. A man my size falls twice as hard when his nerve goes.
dlg.dlg.heini-odermatt.node.recruit.text: A mountain of a man leaning on a halberd taller than himself. "I'm not much for standing my ground alone, {player}, truth told — but shout at my back when the line wavers and I'll hold it all day."
dlg.dlg.heinrich-von-hunenberg.node.idle: A Zug knight, seen only from a wary distance — no words pass between you.
dlg.dlg.heinrich-von-hunenberg.node.warn: Trust the warning — prepare the ambush at Morgarten in earnest.
Distrust it — it could as easily be a trap.

An arrow thuds into the letzi post at dawn, a scrap of parchment bound to the shaft. In Heinrich von Hünenberg's hand, unsigned but unmistakable: "Hütet euch am Morgarten, am Tag vor St. Otmar." Beware at Morgarten, the day before St Otmar's.
"An oversight, Herr Vogt. It won't happen again."
"I answer to the Landsgemeinde, not to a pole."
Say nothing and hold his gaze.
dlg.dlg.hermann-gessler.node.ch1.text: The Landvogt looks you over the way a toll-man weighs a sack. "You've not bowed to my hat, I think. Careless, or deliberate?"
dlg.dlg.hermann-gessler.node.gessler-ang: "Insolence, from a Waldstätte peasant." He signals his guards forward. "We will discuss this properly."
dlg.dlg.hermann-gessler.node.gessler-imp: "Bold words for a valley man." He does not smile. "Mind they do not outlive their welcome — the hat stays on the pole regardless." He waves you on.
dlg.dlg.hohle-gasse-aftermath.node.after: Gessler is down in the sunken road, and his escort — men-at-arms and a few pressed porters both — throw down what they carry.
dlg.dlg.hohle-gasse-aftermath.node.freed: As it is told in Uri: the Landvogt's men who lived that day never forgot who let them walk home.
dlg.dlg.hohle-gasse-aftermath.node.loote: A grim harvest, but a harvest. Gessler's purse is heavier than his reputation deserved.
dlg.dlg.johannes-von-winterthur.node.ch2: A boy of about fourteen, out of place among his father's retinue, watches the Waldstätte lines with plain curiosity rather than fear. "Is it true you fight without knights?" he asks. "My father says that's no way to make war at all."
dlg.dlg.jost-imhof.node.companion.text: Keep to the outside of the switchbacks and mind the scree after rain, {player} — that's the whole of the Gotthard's wisdom, really.
dlg.dlg.jost-imhof.node.recruit.text: A Flüelen muleteer coiling a lead-rope. "You look like you're headed somewhere further than the market, {player}. I know the Gotthard road better than my own father's face — for a fair cut, I'll come along."
dlg.dlg.konrad-ab-yberg.node.argue.choic: Urge restraint — let Stauffacher negotiate first.
dlg.dlg.konrad-ab-yberg.node.argue.text: "Enough charters, enough monks reading us Latin about pastures we've grazed since before their abbey stood." Konrad's fist is white on his staff. "Stauffacher, I say we take back what is ours tonight, Epiphany or no."
dlg.dlg.konrad-ab-yberg.node.ch2-other.t: The abbot's monks still hold pasture that fed my grandfather's cattle, {player}. I have not changed my mind about it.
dlg.dlg.konrad-ab-yberg.node.other.text: A Schwyz man of the Landsgemeinde, not given to soft words. You'll hear plenty from him once the March pastures come up again.
dlg.dlg.leopold-i.node.ch2.text: Seen at a distance across the muster ground at Zug, the Duke does not look your way. His captains do the speaking for him — you are not meant to be this close.
dlg.dlg.marchenstreit-rat.node.argue.cho: Urge restraint — let Stauffacher and the abbot talk first.
dlg.dlg.marchenstreit-rat.node.argue.tex: "Enough of the abbot's Latin," Konrad says, over the noise of the Landsgemeinde hall on the night of the Epiphany. "Schwyz men have grazed the March since before that abbey had a roof. Stauffacher, I say we take back what is ours tonight."
dlg.dlg.marchenstreit-rat.node.argue.var: "Enough of the abbot's Latin," Konrad says — and does not fail to notice Bruder Anselm at your shoulder. "No offence meant to your brother there. But Schwyz men have grazed the March since before that abbey had a roof, and I say we take it back tonight."
dlg.dlg.mechthild-schorno.node.companion: Sit still and let me look at that before it festers, {player}. Bei Sankt Verena, you men never mention the wounds that matter.
dlg.dlg.mechthild-schorno.node.recruit.t: Sorting arnica and yarrow into bundles by her door. "Herbs won't close a halberd wound, but they'll keep a bandaged one from turning. If your road looks like it needs a healer, {player}, I'll come."
dlg.dlg.muster-letzi.node.letzi-strong.t: By the time the first snow falls, the letzi stands higher and thicker than anyone hoped, a full extra course of stone and timber run the length of the Schornen valley floor — a real wall, not a gesture of one.
dlg.dlg.muster-letzi.node.letzi-weak.tex: The wall goes up, serviceable if unlovely — it will hold, though it will not impress anyone who has seen a proper fortification.
dlg.dlg.muster-letzi.node.work.choice.0: Set to work on the wall.
dlg.dlg.muster-letzi.node.work.choice.1: Organise the work-gangs and carry stone yourself.
dlg.dlg.muster-letzi.node.work.text: The letzi wall at Sattel wants raising before the snow makes the work impossible — stone and timber both, and not enough hands who know how to lay either properly.
Send word by the Landsgemeinde messengers instead.
dlg.dlg.muster-recruit.node.call.text: Every valley must send men, and every man sent must be fed, armed, and, ideally, willing. Walking the Landsgemeinde meadows to talk farmers into halberds is its own kind of work.
dlg.dlg.muster-recruit.node.recruit-stro: More men answer the call than the Ammann dared hope — the Schwyz contingent alone swells past what the old counts allowed for, a full two files of spears more than the last levy raised.

More men answer than the Ammann dared hope — though some hedge when Einsiedeln is named, and you hear "plunder" muttered when your back is turned. Two full files of spears more than the last levy, all the same.
More men answer than the Ammann dared hope. Word went round that you held for talk at Einsiedeln, and the hesitant ones come easier for it — a full two files of spears more than the last levy.
dlg.dlg.muster-recruit.node.recruit-thin: You get enough men to matter, though not so many that anyone feels easy about the odds. It will have to do.
You get enough men to matter — fewer than hoped. More than one farmer looks at his boots when Einsiedeln is named. It will have to do.
dlg.dlg.muster-retry.node.return.text: Back at Sattel with what the slope spared you. The letzi still stands — half-built, snow-dusted — and the men who lived are stacking stone again without being told.
dlg.dlg.muster-retry.node.vow.text: "This time," somebody says, not loud, "we hold." Nobody argues.
dlg.dlg.muster-scout.node.scout-caught.t: A sentry's eyes catch yours a moment too long — you get clear of Zug at a dead run before you can count past the knights and the first ranks of footmen. Enough to know it is no small column; not enough to put a firm number to it.
dlg.dlg.muster-scout.node.scout-clean.te: From the hillside above the camp you count it properly and slip out again unseen: knights foremost, then rank on rank of footmen and crossbowmen, then a baggage train long enough that its tail is still making camp when its head has already struck tents — by your best count, some two thousand men, and no mistaking the size of it.
dlg.dlg.muster-scout.node.scout.choice.1: Count the tents from the hillside road without going in.
dlg.dlg.muster-scout.node.scout.text: Zug's streets are thick with Habsburg banners and unfamiliar accents — Duke Leopold's column musters here before it moves, tent-rows enough to count from the hillside if a man is patient and unseen.
dlg.dlg.ritter-eberhard-von-mulinen.node: An Aargau knight in the Duke's column, a coat of plates glinting under a surcoat, eyes the Waldstätte men on the ridgeline the way a hawk eyes a field of mice. He does not speak to peasants.
dlg.dlg.rotzberg-climb.node.slip.text: Your boot scrapes stone loud enough to wake a light sleeper below — the fight that follows is short but not silent. Rotzberg falls all the same, by morning.
dlg.dlg.rotzberg-climb.node.top.text: You are over the wall and among the sleeping garrison before a single man wakes. Rotzberg falls before dawn, as the tellers of Sarnen have it.
Wait for the changing of the watch below the wall.
dlg.dlg.rotzberg-climb.node.wall.text: Under Rotzberg's wall at night, a rope drops from a high window — a servant girl's doing, so the story goes, for love of one of the men below. Climbing it in the dark, in silence, is another matter entirely.
dlg.dlg.ruetli-oath.node.call.text: Torches on the meadow, and the men of three valleys standing in a ring. "Let it be spoken plainly, so none can say after that they did not know the terms." He nods to you. "Speak it, {player} of {origin}, for all to hear."
dlg.dlg.ruetli-oath.node.clause1.text: "I swear: that Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden shall stand by one another with aid, counsel and every kindness — within the valleys and without — against any man who does violence or wrong to one of us, or to our goods."
dlg.dlg.ruetli-oath.node.clause2.text: "I swear further: that we shall accept no judge in these matters who is not himself of the land and dwelling among us, nor one who has bought his office — no stranger, and no man's purse, sent to rule where it does not belong."
dlg.dlg.ruetli-oath.node.clause3.text: "And where any quarrel rises among us, it shall be laid before the most prudent among the sworn, and settled by their judgment — the sword kept sheathed until judgment fails."
dlg.dlg.ruetli-oath.node.close.text: "So sworn." He sets Schwyz's own seal to the warm wax — not his ring, the Land's — and Uri and Unterwalden's witnesses ready theirs beside it. "Now it is not one man's word, or three. It is the Länder's."
dlg.dlg.saeumer-crossing.node.across.tex: Every mule makes it across without losing its footing — a clean crossing, and Niklaus claps you on the shoulder for it.
dlg.dlg.saeumer-crossing.node.bridge.cho: Unload the worst mule and lead it across empty.
dlg.dlg.saeumer-crossing.node.bridge.tex: The Teufelsbrücke spans the gorge in a single narrow arch, spray from the falls slicking the timber underfoot. One mule already balks at the noise.
dlg.dlg.saeumer-crossing.node.stumble.te: A mule's load shifts badly on the narrow footing and a salt sack goes into the gorge before you can steady it — the rest make it across, at least.
dlg.dlg.saeumer-escort.node.depart.text: "Good. Keep to the outside of the bends and mind the mules — they'll balk before you see the danger yourself, half the time."
dlg.dlg.saeumer-escort.node.offer.choice: "The pass is no place for me this season."
dlg.dlg.saeumer-escort.node.offer.text: The muleteer checks a last girth strap. "Salt and cloth for Ursern, over the Schöllenen — and the Teufelsbrücke's footing is treacherous since the spring melt. An extra pair of eyes wouldn't go amiss, {player}."
dlg.dlg.sarnen-procession.node.gift.choi: Carry a basket in and keep your face pleasant.
Hang back with the last baskets and slip in unnoticed.
dlg.dlg.sarnen-procession.node.gift.text: New Year's morning: Sarnen's men form a procession up to Landenberg's hill bearing gift baskets for the bailiff — hams, cheeses, and, hidden under the linen, halberds broken down to fit.
dlg.dlg.sarnen-procession.node.inside.te: Landenberg accepts his gifts with a bailiff's customary graciousness, never once suspecting the linen. When the baskets open, the hill is yours before he finds his sword.
dlg.dlg.sarnen-procession.node.suspiciou: A guard eyes your basket a moment too long — but the halberds are already coming out from under the linen by the time he decides to say something.
dlg.dlg.schuetzenkoenig-contest.node.sho: Dead centre — the crowd goes quiet a moment before it cheers. You are, for this market day at least, Schützenkönig.
A good shot, but not the winning one — you place well enough to be remembered, if not crowned.
Shoot steadily rather than for the crown.
The mark stands eighty paces off, ringed in chalk. A dozen Uri men have already tried and missed the centre.
dlg.dlg.schuetzenkoenig-entry.node.enter: "Good. The mark's at eighty paces, same distance they say Tell shot from — though nobody's foolish enough to put an apple on a head for this one."
dlg.dlg.schuetzenkoenig-entry.node.entry: "My bolt is spoken for elsewhere, Burkhard."
"We're holding a shoot by the lime tree come market day, {player} — every man in Uri with a crossbow worth the name is entering. Let's see if your aim matches your talk."
dlg.dlg.ueli-zgraggen.node.companion.tex: A shield wall holds only as long as the man on the end of it, {player}. Watch the flanks — I learned that lesson from the wrong side of it once.
dlg.dlg.ueli-zgraggen.node.recruit.text: Leaning against the tavern wall, a Habsburg-pattern shield still on his back though the surcoat is long gone. "I know how their sergeants think, {player}, because I used to be paid to think that way myself. Worth something to you?"
dlg.dlg.vogt-schreiber-ludwig.node.ch1.t: Gessler's clerk squints up from his ledger. "Toll's two Pfennig for the bridge, or twenty if you'd rather I mark you down as one of the hat's enemies. Your choice, freely given."
dlg.dlg.walter-fuerst.node.ch1.text: My kinsman keeps his own counsel about that hat on the pole, {player}. I worry for him more than he lets on.
dlg.dlg.walter-fuerst.node.ch1.variant.0: Mind how you pass the square today, {player}. The Vogt's men are watching close, and I'd rather not visit you in the tower.
dlg.dlg.walter-fuerst.node.ch1.variant.1: I heard you bowed to the hat, {player}. No shame in it — a bent knee costs less than a broken one.
dlg.dlg.walter-fuerst.node.ch1.variant.2: They say you walked that square and talked your own way clear of the guards after, {player}. My kinsman would have liked to see that.
dlg.dlg.walter-fuerst.node.ch2.text: I am too old for the letzi wall now, but my grandsons are not, and neither are you. Bei Sankt Verena, watch yourself at Sattel.
dlg.dlg.walter-fuerst.node.message.choic: "I'll carry it to him myself, Herr Fürst."
dlg.dlg.walter-fuerst.node.message.text: You'll be the one from Flüelen with word of the King's death, then. Good. Freiherr von Attinghausen must hear it before the rumour beats you there — and there's a boat leaving for Steinen besides, if you're minded to see this through.
dlg.dlg.walter-fuerst.node.prologue-othe: Altdorf is astir since the news came down from Flüelen. Find the Freiherr, if you've not already — he'll want to hear it plainly, not third-hand.
dlg.dlg.werner-stauffacher.node.ch1-hous: Well enough — though a Vogt's clerk came asking after the seal of Schwyz again. They do not forget which Land sealed first.
dlg.dlg.werner-stauffacher.node.ch1-reso: What we swore on the Rütli, we hold to. When Uri and Unterwalden move, Schwyz will not be found wanting.
dlg.dlg.werner-stauffacher.node.ch1.choi: What will Schwyz do about it?
How fares your house at Steinen?
dlg.dlg.werner-stauffacher.node.ch1.text: Sixteen years since the Rütli, {player}, and still that hat sits on its pole. My own household tells me I brood on it too much.
dlg.dlg.werner-stauffacher.node.ch1.vari: There was steel over that hat, {player}, and your name on it. Schwyz remembers who bleeds early — mind the Vogt does too.
dlg.dlg.werner-stauffacher.node.ch2-prep: The letzi at Sattel wants stone yet, and every third man still fights with a scythe re-hafted for war. We will manage. We always have.
dlg.dlg.werner-stauffacher.node.ch2.text: Grey in the beard now, {player} of {origin}, and still they call me Ammann. Leopold musters at Zug — I feel it in my knees before I hear it from the scouts.
dlg.dlg.werner-stauffacher.node.ch2.vari: Hold the slope when the day comes, {player}. I mean to command from the Haufen's front rank, not behind it.
dlg.dlg.werner-stauffacher.node.prologue: The Landsgemeinde is called. You are asked to come.
A freeman of Steinen you find sharpening a scythe. "News from Altdorf, {player}? Then it is true — the King is dead, and the Länder must look to themselves."
dlg.dlg.werner-von-attinghausen.node.ch1: I counsel patience where Werner Stauffacher counsels the sword, {player}. Which of us is right, the years ahead will show — I only hope the showing costs us little.
Word reached me that you bowed to the hat, {player}. A wise-enough head for a bad season — I do not fault it.
Word reached me that you walked past the hat and reasoned your way clear of the guards after, {player}. A cool head in a watched square — Uri needs more of those than of drawn steel.
They tell me you stood by and watched Tell refuse that hat, {player}, and said nothing yourself. A cautious man's way through a dangerous morning.
I heard there was steel drawn in the square over that hat, {player}, and your name attached to it. The Vogt will remember it, and so will I.
dlg.dlg.werner-von-attinghausen.node.ch2: I am too old now for the letzi wall, but Uri's men march regardless, and my blessing goes with them, for what an old man's blessing is worth.
dlg.dlg.werner-von-attinghausen.node.mee: There will be. Steinen, or near it — word will reach you. Go carefully, and go quietly; not every ear on the road loves us.
dlg.dlg.werner-von-attinghausen.node.pro: The house of Attinghausen has stood by Uri since before any charter was written, {player}. While my name still carries weight in the valley, no bailiff rules here unchallenged. That much I intend to keep true.
dlg.dlg.werner-von-attinghausen.node.rec: "Walter Fürst says there will be a meeting."
The Freiherr receives you in his hall without ceremony. "King Rudolf dead, you say. Then the question is not whether Vienna forgets us — it is whether we let it."
dlg.dlg.wilhelm-tell.node.campfire-after: "Uri owes you more than it can pay."
Gessler's dead in the ditch, {player}, and Bürglen smells the same as ever from here. Burn the strongholds if you must — my part of this was one bolt, and it is spent.
dlg.dlg.wilhelm-tell.node.campfire-eve.t: Fire's low, {player}. Tomorrow Gessler rides the sunken road, and my bolt will be waiting. I have shot it twice already in my head — once for him, once for the miss I will not make.
dlg.dlg.wilhelm-tell.node.companion.text: Every crossing on this lake, I know its temper, {player}. Say the word if you need a bolt loosed instead of a boat rowed.
dlg.dlg.wilhelm-tell.node.general.text: Bürglen keeps me fed on venison and lets me be, mostly. That hat on the Altdorf pole is the Vogt's idea of a joke, and a poor one.
dlg.dlg.wilhelm-tell.node.steady-grim.te: Watch or not, it happens the same. Stand back, then, and let me work.
Then stand where I can see you and say nothing more. The wind is worse than the range.
"Your hand is steadier than any man's in Uri. Trust it."
dlg.dlg.wilhelm-tell.node.steady.text: They've set my boy against the tree, {player}, an apple on his crown, and Gessler counting the paces off himself. Say something useful or say nothing at all.
dlg.dlg.zwing-uri-stealth.node.gate.choi: Talk your way past the gate guard instead.
Scout the gate from the treeline first, then decide.
dlg.dlg.zwing-uri-stealth.node.gate.text: Zwing Uri stands half-built above Amsteg, timber scaffolding still up one wall. A file of labourers carries stone in through the unfinished gate every morning — no one looks twice at another back bent under a load.
dlg.dlg.zwing-uri-stealth.node.inside.te: Once inside, the half-finished walls give you every advantage — the garrison surrenders the half-built keep without much of a fight once they see how many of "the labourers" have thrown down their sacks for weapons.
dlg.dlg.zwing-uri-stealth.node.noticed.t: A guard's eyes narrow at you a beat too long — but by the time he calls out, you and enough others are already past him. Zwing Uri falls, messier than it might have, but it falls.
quest.quest.alpstreit.description: A Sattel farmer asks you to arbitrate a boundary dispute with the Arth herders — the Bundesbrief promises judgment before the sword.
quest.quest.alpstreit.stage.hearing.jour: Both sides lay their claims before you on the disputed slope.
quest.quest.alpstreit.stage.offer.journa: Melchior Arnold of Sattel complains that the Arth herders keep moving the boundary stones.
quest.quest.alpstreit.stage.ruling.journ: The boundary is settled — for now.
quest.quest.alpstreit.title: Alpstreit
quest.quest.bad-zu-wolfenschiessen.descr: A Wolfenschiessen farmer asks for help keeping quiet what happened to a bailiff's man in the bath-house.
quest.quest.bad-zu-wolfenschiessen.onSta: Quest started: Das Bad zu Wolfenschiessen
quest.quest.bad-zu-wolfenschiessen.stage: A body wants a quiet grave before dawn.
Jost Durrer of Wolfenschiessen hints at a killing best kept quiet.
By first light, there is nothing left to find.
quest.quest.bad-zu-wolfenschiessen.title: Das Bad zu Wolfenschiessen
quest.quest.brunnen-1315.description: At Brunnen, the Bundesbrief is renewed — this time in German. Act 1 ends here.
quest.quest.brunnen-1315.onStart.0: Quest started: Der Pakt von Brunnen
quest.quest.brunnen-1315.stage.pact.jour: The quay at Brunnen fills for the renewal of the covenant.
quest.quest.brunnen-1315.stage.travel-br: Word goes out to gather at Brunnen for the renewal of the covenant.
quest.quest.brunnen-1315.title: Der Pakt von Brunnen
quest.quest.burgenbruch.description: Three strongholds must fall before spring: half-built Zwing Uri, Rotzberg above Stans, and Landenberg's hill at Sarnen.
By spring, all three strongholds have fallen — told in Sarnen ever after as the Burgenbruch.
quest.quest.burgenbruch.stage.choose.jou: Three strongholds await: Zwing Uri by the Gotthard road, Rotzberg above Stans, and Landenberg's hill at Sarnen.
quest.quest.burgenbruch.stage.choose.obj: Storm at least one stronghold yourself, or send trusted companions to the rest.
quest.quest.burgenbruch.stage.rotzberg.j: Rotzberg's wall rises above you in the dark.
quest.quest.burgenbruch.stage.sarnen.jou: The gift procession forms up below Landenberg's hill.
quest.quest.burgenbruch.stage.travel-rot: You set out for Rotzberg, above Stans, to climb its wall by night.
quest.quest.burgenbruch.stage.travel-sar: You set out to join the New Year's gift procession into Sarnen, weapons hidden in the baskets.
Make for Landenberg's hill at Sarnen.
quest.quest.burgenbruch.stage.travel-zwi: You set out for Zwing Uri, half-built above Amsteg.
Zwing Uri stands half-built above Amsteg, ready to be taken.
quest.quest.burgenbruch.title: Burgenbruch
quest.quest.der-eid.description: News of King Rudolf's death reaches the Waldstätte. Carry word, escort an elder to the meeting, and stand witness as the Bundesbrief is sealed.
quest.quest.der-eid.onComplete.0: The Bundesbrief is sealed. Sixteen years pass...
quest.quest.der-eid.stage.altdorf-messag: The Landsgemeinde is called at Altdorf. Walter Fürst asks you to carry word to Freiherr Werner von Attinghausen.
Find Walter Fürst at Altdorf and carry his message.
quest.quest.der-eid.stage.escort-recover: The toll-men beat you back from the quay. The elder's boat pulls off to a hidden inlet to wait out the hour — you will have to try the quay again.
Regroup and try the Brunnen quay again.
quest.quest.der-eid.stage.escort.journal: A boat carries the elder toward Steinen and the meeting place — but the Brunnen quay road is not always safe for Habsburg toll-men to travel unchallenged, nor for those who cross them.
quest.quest.der-eid.stage.escort.objecti: Escort the elder past the Brunnen quay.
quest.quest.der-eid.stage.fluelen-news.j: Flüelen, dawn: a Säumer boat brings word that King Rudolf of Habsburg is dead.
quest.quest.der-eid.stage.fluelen-news.o: Learn the news at Flüelen, then make for Altdorf.
quest.quest.der-eid.stage.ruetli-oath.jo: Night falls on the Rütli meadow. Werner Stauffacher, Walter Fürst and Arnold von Melchtal — and their witnesses — gather to swear.
quest.quest.der-eid.stage.ruetli-oath.ob: Speak the oath at the Rütli.
quest.quest.der-eid.stage.sealing.journa: The letter is drawn up to be sealed.
quest.quest.der-eid.stage.sealing.object: Witness the sealing of the Bundesbrief.
Word passes quietly: gather at the Rütli meadow after dark.
quest.quest.der-eid.title: Der Eid
quest.quest.der-hut.description: Sixteen years on: a Habsburg hat on a pole in Altdorf, a crossbowman who will not bow to it, and the storming of three strongholds before winter.
quest.quest.der-hut.onStart.0: Quest started: Der Hut auf der Stange
quest.quest.der-hut.stage.aftermath.jour: Gessler is dead in the Hohle Gasse — as it is told in Uri.
quest.quest.der-hut.stage.aftermath.obje: Decide what becomes of the Landvogt's escort.
quest.quest.der-hut.stage.altdorf-pole.j: Gessler's hat stands over the square, and Vogt-Schreiber Ludwig watches who bows to it.
quest.quest.der-hut.stage.altdorf-pole.o: Decide how to pass Gessler's hat.
quest.quest.der-hut.stage.apple-shot.jou: Wilhelm Tell refuses to bow. Gessler sets him a test: shoot an apple from his own son's head.
quest.quest.der-hut.stage.apple-shot.obj: Speak with Tell before the shot.
quest.quest.der-hut.stage.burgenbruch.jo: Word goes out through the Länder: before spring, the strongholds at Zwing Uri, Rotzberg and Sarnen must fall.
quest.quest.der-hut.stage.epilogue.journ: The bailiffs are gone from Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden. Tell goes back to Bürglen and his crossbow.
quest.quest.der-hut.stage.hohle-gasse-re: The escort drives you back up the sunken road. Tell pulls back into the trees to wait for a second chance.
Regroup and hold the Hohle Gasse again.
quest.quest.der-hut.stage.hohle-gasse.jo: Tell waits in the sunken road for Gessler. The party holds the road behind him.
quest.quest.der-hut.stage.hohle-gasse.ob: Hold the Hohle Gasse while Tell's shot resolves.
quest.quest.der-hut.stage.tellsplatte.jo: A storm on the Urnersee gives Tell his chance.
quest.quest.der-hut.stage.tellsplatte.ob: Witness the leap at the Tellsplatte.
quest.quest.der-hut.stage.travel-altdorf: Sixteen years since the Rütli. Word from Altdorf says a hat now sits on a pole by the lime tree, and every man is made to bow to it — though the tellers of Sarnen, setting this down long after, give no year for it.
Make for Altdorf and see the hat for yourself.
quest.quest.der-hut.stage.travel-hohle-g: Word reaches you: Tell means to wait for Gessler in the sunken road toward Küssnacht.
quest.quest.der-hut.stage.travel-tellspl: Arrested regardless of the shot, Tell is carried toward Küssnacht by boat.
Follow the boat down the Urnersee toward the Tellsplatte.
quest.quest.der-hut.title: Der Hut auf der Stange
quest.quest.der-saeumer.description: Lead a Säumer mule train up the Gotthard road and through the Schöllenen gorge, past the treacherous footing of the Teufelsbrücke.
quest.quest.der-saeumer.stage.crossing.j: Spray from the falls slicks the bridge timber underfoot.
quest.quest.der-saeumer.stage.offer.jour: Niklaus Planzer of Amsteg asks for an extra pair of eyes on the road to Ursern.
quest.quest.der-saeumer.stage.reward.jou: The train reaches Andermatt safe, more or less.
quest.quest.der-saeumer.stage.schoellene: The road climbs into the Schöllenen gorge, toward the Teufelsbrücke.
Lead the train to the Teufelsbrücke.
quest.quest.der-saeumer.title: Der Säumer
quest.quest.drache-vom-pilatus.descripti: An innkeeper in Luzern asks you to look into rumours of a "dragon" seen circling Pilatus.
quest.quest.drache-vom-pilatus.onStart.0: Quest started: Der Drache vom Pilatus
quest.quest.drache-vom-pilatus.stage.cli: The alp of Pilatus rises above the Luzern basin.
quest.quest.drache-vom-pilatus.stage.off: Trudi Meier of Luzern relays a rumour of a dragon over Pilatus.
quest.quest.drache-vom-pilatus.stage.res: No dragon — a lammergeier, and a smuggler's cache.
quest.quest.drache-vom-pilatus.stage.tru: Something large circles the high cliffs.
quest.quest.drache-vom-pilatus.title: Der Drache vom Pilatus
quest.quest.epilog-1308.description: Word arrives from the Aargau: King Albrecht I is dead, murdered by his own nephew. Habsburg pressure on the Länder pauses.
quest.quest.epilog-1308.onStart.0: News reaches the valleys: King Albrecht I is dead.
quest.quest.epilog-1308.stage.news.journ: A rider comes in from the Aargau, road-worn and grim-faced.
quest.quest.epilog-1308.title: News from Windisch
quest.quest.fischer-von-gersau.descripti: Gersau's fishermen answer to no lord, yet the Brunnen toll-men stop their fish carts on the shore road all the same.
quest.quest.fischer-von-gersau.onStart.0: Quest started: Die Fischer von Gersau
quest.quest.fischer-von-gersau.stage.con: The toll-man Konrad Niederberger holds the Brunnen quay road.
quest.quest.fischer-von-gersau.stage.res: Gersau's fish carts pass unmolested — for now.
quest.quest.fischer-von-gersau.stage.tro: Uli Fischer of Gersau complains of Habsburg toll-men harassing the fish carts.
quest.quest.fischer-von-gersau.title: Die Fischer von Gersau
quest.quest.marchenstreit.description: On the night of the Epiphany, the old quarrel over the March pastures breaks into the open. Schwyz argues for raiding Einsiedeln abbey.
quest.quest.marchenstreit.stage.aftermat: Within weeks, word comes down from the bishop: the Confederates stand excommunicated over the abbey affair.
quest.quest.marchenstreit.stage.epiphany: The night of the Heiligen Drei Könige, 1314: Konrad Ab Yberg and Werner Stauffacher argue in the Schwyz Landsgemeinde hall over the March pastures.
Hear the argument and choose a side.
quest.quest.marchenstreit.stage.raid.jou: The raiding party moves on Einsiedeln abbey before dawn — plunder, and monks dragged back to Schwyz.
quest.quest.marchenstreit.stage.speech-p: You press for restraint. Abbot Johannes agrees to hear terms before Schwyz's men take matters further.
quest.quest.marchenstreit.stage.travel-e: Word carries ahead of you, toward Einsiedeln.
quest.quest.marchenstreit.title: Marchenstreit
quest.quest.morgarten.description: Duke Leopold's column marches from Zug along the Ägerisee toward Schwyz. The Confederates hold the slope above the road.
quest.quest.morgarten.stage.aftermath.jo: The column is broken. Leopold is away toward Zug before the rout is done.
quest.quest.morgarten.stage.battle.journ: 15 November, 1315. The column comes on between the lake and the slope, and the boulder caches wait above the road.
quest.quest.morgarten.stage.battle.objec: Hold the slope, then rout the column at Morgarten.
The line breaks and you are carried off the field, bleeding, as the column presses on toward Schwyz. It will have to be faced again — and better prepared.
quest.quest.morgarten.stage.travel-morga: The muster marches for the Morgarten slope, above the road from Ägeri.
Take position on the Morgarten slope.
quest.quest.morgarten.title: Morgarten
quest.quest.muster-1315.description: A year of readiness: strengthen the letzi at Sattel, recruit, scout Leopold's muster at Zug, and weigh the Hünenberg warning.
quest.quest.muster-1315.onStart.0: Quest started: Das Jahr der Rüstung
An unsigned arrow strikes the letzi post at dawn, a warning bound to the shaft.
Decide whether to trust Hünenberg's warning.
quest.quest.muster-1315.stage.letzi-craf: The letzi wall at Sattel must be raised before the snow makes the work impossible.
quest.quest.muster-1315.stage.ready.jour: The muster is as ready as it will ever be. Word comes that Leopold's column has begun to move.
quest.quest.muster-1315.stage.recruit.jo: Every valley must send men to the muster.
quest.quest.muster-1315.stage.sattel-ret: Carried off once at Morgarten, you gather what is left and ready the muster again.
Speak with the survivors at Sattel.
Duke Leopold's column musters at Zug.
Scout the Habsburg muster at Zug.
quest.quest.muster-1315.stage.travel-sat: A year of readiness begins. The letzi at Sattel needs raising before the work becomes impossible in the snow.
Make for the letzi at Sattel.
quest.quest.muster-1315.stage.travel-zug: Word says Duke Leopold's column is mustering at Zug — someone must see how many they are.
quest.quest.muster-1315.title: Das Jahr der Rüstung
quest.quest.schuetzenkoenig.description: A crossbow contest by the Altdorf lime tree, eighty paces — the same distance as the legend.
quest.quest.schuetzenkoenig.stage.contes: The mark stands eighty paces off, ringed in chalk.
Burkhard Wyrsch invites you to enter the Altdorf shooting contest.
quest.quest.schuetzenkoenig.title: Schützenkönig
